title: Fit a B22 bulb into a ceiling pendant's lampholder that hangs free on its flex
instruction: Fit the new bulb into the hanging pendant lampholder so it locks in.
context: Changing a bulb in a ceiling pendant is one of the most common jobs in a home: the bare lampholder hangs on its flex, and a B22 bayonet bulb goes in by pushing it up against two spring plungers, turning it about 15 degrees and letting it drop into the hooks of two J-slots. The holder hangs from a soft flex, so it has nothing to push against: pushed from below it simply rises, and turned it spins round on the flex. People hold the lampholder still with one hand and push and turn the bulb with the other. Here a stand at the robot's working height stands in for the ceiling, and the pendant is not wired. What goes wrong: the bulb pushed up with no hand on the holder, so the holder rides up and the pins never reach the hooks; the holder turned instead of the bulb, winding the flex; the holder pulled down hard, straining the flex at the ceiling rose; the bulb let go before its pins are in the hooks, so it drops out.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; heights from the table top. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +305 and -305 mm. (1) A rigid stand standing in for the ceiling: a 30 mm square steel post at x 450 mm, y 0 on a foot plate, with a top arm reaching back to x 260 mm, y 0, its underside 500 mm up; fixed to the table, nothing on it within 100 mm of the lampholder. (2) A plain white plastic pendant set hanging from the arm: a ceiling rose (est 75 mm across, 30 mm deep) under the arm at x 300 mm, y 0, 0.75 mm2 round two-core white flex (est 6 mm across), and a B22d plastic lampholder to BS EN 61184, mouth down. Estimates (est): lampholder 38 mm across, 52 mm long, 30 g, friction 0.5; flex 240 mm from rose to holder, so the mouth hangs 178 mm up. The flex swings freely, buckles when the holder is pushed up (it rises up to 40 mm before the flex resists), stretches at 600 N/m when pulled down and turns the holder back by 0.0005 N m per degree of twist. Mechanism (est): a 28 mm bore with a 25.5 mm collar at its top that keeps the cap's end near the axis; two J-slots 180 degrees apart; two long, soft spring plungers in the base, 5 mm of travel, pushing down with 0.4 N each at rest and 0.45 N each at full travel. The bulb's pins go up the J's vertical legs, are pushed at least 3 mm up against the plungers (5 mm to their stop), turned 15 degrees and drop onto the hook floors, 2 mm up the plungers' travel, each between two 1 mm lips, where the plungers hold them. (3) A new Philips LED Classic A60 B22 bulb, frosted, standing cap-up in a 50 mm tall ring stand fixed to the table at x 250 mm, y -130 mm, its pins lined up with the J's legs (matching paint marks on the cap and the stand). Published: 60 mm across, B22d cap (22 mm, two pins). Estimates (est): 104 mm long, 40 g. Friction (est): bulb glass on gripper 0.8. Nothing else is on the table. (4) Acceptance checks on the bought pendant before the first trial (0-2 N and 0-10 N spring scales, kitchen scale, ruler): pushing a bulb up to the plungers' stop with the holder held takes 1.5 N or less; let go, a locked bulb stays in under a 5 N pull; the cap and mouth carry matching paint marks at the entry angle; the holder weighs under 50 g; the flex hangs 220 to 260 mm. A pendant that fails a check is not used.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the poses of the lampholder, its plungers and hook floors, the bulb and both grippers. Locked: both bulb pins in the hooks of their J-slots (both hook floors 80% or more of their travel in under the pins), the bulb turned 13 to 17 degrees from the J's leg, its cap's end within 0.5 mm of where the pins rest on the hook floor (2 mm up the plungers' travel), and its axis within 5 degrees and 1.5 mm of the holder's. Released: on every step of the last 1 s no gripper's finger zone (a capsule round the last 38 mm of its fingers, larger than the fingers) within 2 mm of the bulb or the holder. Hanging: over the last 1 s the holder's mouth moved under 10 mm, and it is within 30 mm (top view) and 15 mm (height) of where it hung at the start. Dropped (latched): after the bulb has left its ring stand (lifted 8 mm), its lowest point within 2 mm of the table, or its globe (a 60 mm sphere) within 1 mm of either stand, set back in its ring included. Strained (latched): at any step the mouth more than 15 mm below where it hung at the start (the flex pulled tight against the rose). Wound (latched): at any step the holder turned more than 90 degrees about its flex from where it hung at the start. Score 0 if dropped, or the bulb is not locked. Otherwise 0.25 if strained; else 0.5 if wound; else 1.0 if released and hanging; else 0.5. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial (the pendant is not wired: the rose is a dummy and nothing is live), per condition: locked, after the trial a 5 N spring-scale pull straight down does not bring the bulb out, and a paint mark on the cap sits 15 degrees round from the matching mark at the mouth (a bulb whose pins are not in the hooks falls out or turns back); released and hanging, 30 fps front video of the whole trial, read over its last 1 s, with a 10 mm scale on the stand beside the holder; dropped, the whole-trial video (any contact of the bulb with the table or a stand after it leaves its ring stand); strained, a 15 mm mark on the stand at the holder's resting height, checked on every frame of the whole-trial video; wound, a stripe painted down the holder and flex, checked on every frame of the same video (more than a quarter turn counts). How many tries it takes is not penalised.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The flex is a joint chain (est): two swing hinges at the rose, a free 40 mm slack slide, a 600 N/m stretch spring and the holder's twist spring. The plungers are sprung slides, softer than a real holder's (est) to suit the simulated arms; the bore, collar, plungers, hook floors and lips are contact. The J-slot's shape is a declared rule: it slides the hook floors in under the pins once they have gone up the leg and turned at the top, and back out when the pins leave.
reset_notes: Push the bulb up, turn it back 15 degrees and lower it out of the holder; stand it cap-up in its ring stand at x 250 mm, y -130 mm with its paint mark on the stand's. Let the holder hang still with its painted stripe to the front. Nothing is consumed; between trials check that the flex has no twist (stripe straight) and that a bulb locks and stays in under a 5 N pull.
